title: California's 32nd Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The general election for California's 32nd Congressional District pits 15-term Democratic incumbent Brad Sherman against Republican entertainment lawyer and film producer Larry Thompson. The district covers western San Fernando Valley communities including Sherman Oaks, Woodland Hills, and Tarzana, as well as Malibu and other coastal areas, plus Simi Valley in Ventura County following mid-decade redistricting. With a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+14 and over 46% Democratic registered voters, the seat is rated Solid D by the Cook Political Report, but Sherman faced a competitive primary challenge from fellow Democrat Jake Levine before advancing. Thompson, who was unanimously endorsed by the California Republican Party in 2024 and advanced from the top-two primary as the sole Republican candidate, is making his second consecutive bid for this seat after losing to Sherman in the 2024 general election.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the Sherman-Thompson general election matchup in California's 32nd Congressional District as of mid-June 2026. The primary election was held on June 2, 2026.

candidates.name: Brad Sherman
candidates.summary: Brad Sherman is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 32nd Congressional District, first elected in 1996 and currently serving his 15th term. He serves as a senior member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the House Financial Services Committee, and was a leader in creating the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. Sherman previously served on the California State Board of Equalization from 1991 to 1996, including as chair from 1991 to 1995.

candidates.name: Larry Thompson
candidates.summary: Larry Thompson is a Republican candidate running for U.S. House in California's 32nd Congressional District. He is an entertainment lawyer, talent manager, and film producer who founded the Larry A. Thompson Organization, and has managed the careers of over 250 entertainers. Thompson served in the U.S. Army Reserve's Judge Advocate General's Corps from 1968 to 1974 and was the unanimously endorsed Republican candidate for this seat in 2024 before advancing from the 2026 top-two primary to face incumbent Brad Sherman in the general election.
